football_evidence.question: Can Rutgers contain Northwestern’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.1 points.
supporting: When Northwestern has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Northwestern’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.9% of its dropbacks, and Rutgers’ defense sacks the quarterback on 4.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Rutgers’ offensive line No. 28 nationally and Northwestern’s No. 86.
When Rutgers has the ball (third down): Rutgers’ offense converts 47.1% of its third downs, and Northwestern’s defense allows opponents to convert 36.2% of their third downs (FBS average 39.7%).

When Rutgers has the ball (down-to-down efficiency): Rutgers’ offense succeeds on 47.6% of its offensive plays, and Northwestern’s defense allows opponents to succeed on 42.4% of their plays (FBS average 42.4%).
contradicting: When Northwestern has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Northwestern’s offense averages 5.6 yards per carry, and Rutgers’ defense allows 6.8 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Northwestern has the ball (big plays through the air): Northwestern’s offense turns 15.8% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Rutgers’ defense gives up explosive gains on 10.9% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When Northwestern has the ball (big plays on the ground): Northwestern’s offense turns 9.1% of its runs into explosive gains, and Rutgers’ defense gives up explosive gains on 11.1% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Northwestern has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Northwestern’s offense averages 9.6 yards per pass attempt, and Rutgers’ defense allows 7.5 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
quarterbacks: Aidan Chiles has completed 98 of 142 passes (69.0%) for 1,398 yards, 9.8 yards per attempt, 9 touchdowns and no interceptions in six games for Northwestern, and has been sacked on 14 of 156 dropbacks.
Dylan Lonergan has completed 74 of 127 passes (58.3%) for 1,066 yards, 8.4 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in five games for Rutgers, and has been sacked on 6 of 133 dropbacks.
AJ Surace has completed 33 of 53 passes (62.3%) for 475 yards, 9.0 yards per attempt, 6 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in four games for Rutgers, and has been sacked on 8 of 61 dropbacks.

model: Rutgers’ defense has to come out ahead on long runs: it gives up explosive gains on 11.1% of opponent runs, against an offense that turns 9.1% of its runs into explosive gains.
Rutgers’ defense has to slow Northwestern on big pass plays — Northwestern’s offense turns 15.8% of its pass plays into explosive gains.
Rutgers’ defense has to come out ahead in the pass-rush matchup: it sacks the quarterback on 4.6% of opponent dropbacks, against an offense that has allowed a sack on 8.9% of its dropbacks.
Rutgers’ offense has to keep winning on third down: it converts 47.1% of its third downs, and Northwestern’s defense allows opponents to convert 36.2% of their third downs.
